headline.title: First flakes for Northern Vermont.
headline.text: Up to {{s:1}} on the summit of Jay Peak Friday morning to early Saturday. All 19 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Northern Vermont. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

sevensprings.headline: Freeze Watch issued October 16 at 12:30PM EDT until October 18 at 9:00AM EDT by NWS State College PA
sevensprings.text: * WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 25 possible. * WHERE...A portion of central Pennsylvania. * WHEN...From late Saturday night through Sunday morning. * IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor plumbing.

BTV.excerpt:
A strong storm system will bring widespread rain and gusty winds today, followed by much colder weather and mountain snow showers on Saturday.
Next week continues to look very quiet with temperatures near normal and high confidence of an extended dry period of weather.

ALY.excerpt:
) A strong cold front will bring gusty winds, showers, and a few thunderstorms to the region today. Continued gusty and unseasonably chilly conditions are expected tonight into Saturday. A coating of snow is possible in the high terrain late tonight into Saturday morning.
) Dry weather with temperatures moderating to near seasonable levels Sunday into early next week.

GYX.excerpt:
Periods of rain today with a brief thunderstorm possible in New Hampshire this afternoon.
A seasonably cold airmass arrives to start the weekend, with wintry conditions across the higher terrain.
Mild and dry conditions look to persist from Sunday through much of next week as high pressure dominates over the Northeast.

PHI.excerpt:
A warm front moves north through the region this morning, followed by a strong cold front this afternoon and evening.
Widespread frost and freeze conditions are increasingly likely Saturday night.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Just a coating for the high peaks.
paras: Light snow Friday morning to early Saturday: Jay Peak {{s:1}}, Stowe {{s:0.7}}, Sugarbush {{s:0.5}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0.2,4.9}} at Jay Peak. Rain mixes in even up high at times.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:20}} to {{t:56}}, with up to {{s:1.9}} of snow and gusts near {{w:44}} up top.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 27).
NWS Burlington forecasters, Friday 7:36 AM: "A strong storm system will bring widespread rain and gusty winds today, followed by much colder weather and mountain snow showers on Saturday."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.

insights.text: First flakes: about {{s:1}} at the summit Friday morning to early Saturday (models {{r:0.2,4.9}}). It starts as rain ({{l:1.09}}), even at the summit, then changes to snow Friday night as colder air arrives. It won't last: highs reach {{t:48}} Monday.
Cold enough to make snow Saturday morning to Sunday morning: about 27 hours at or below {{t:26}} at mid-mountain, counting humidity. Whether the guns run is up to the resort.
Typically opens around Nov 27, 42 days out.
